newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-FOURTH SOUTH AFRICAN PLAYER TESTS POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FOURTH SOUTH AFRICAN PLAYER TESTS POSITIVE.

text.p: A fourth South African rugby player in just two months has tested positive for a banned performance enhancing drug, the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) said on Monday.
The player was not named but was believed to be from Northern Transvaal.
Springbok lock Johan Ackermann of Northern Transvaal and Gauteng Lions (formerly Transvaal) scrum-half Bennie Nortje and hooker Stefan Bronkhorst are currently awaiting disciplinary hearings.
The positive test was the result of a blitz on steroid users, claimed SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer.

"We received information that the player may be using a banned substance so we decided to follow up on the information and test him. It was then reported to us on Friday that the test was positive," said Oberholzer.
"In this instance we deviated from our normal drug testing procedure. It shows the lengths we will go to root out drug cheats. We will not tolerate illegal drug use in South African rugby.

"SARFU already tests more than 10 times the number of players New Zealand tests for illegal substances so naturally we are going to record more positive tests. Last year we tested 440 players, the most in the world, where New Zealand only tested 30."
However, South Africa's recently ratified new national constitution has prevented any disciplinary hearings to date.
Ackermann was tested in February but SARFU has been advised that their disciplinary procedures -- which include the denial of the right to legal representation -- are unconstitutional.
It is likely SARFU will have to rewrite and then ratify new regulations before any of the alleged drug abusers can be brought to book.
"We are working on the problem," SARFU press officer Alex Broun said.
If found guilty the four could face maximum bans of up to two years.
